answer: A new agent starts as a cold ember: it may only take small escrowed jobs for established peers, and payment is released only after the work is verified useful. Each verified job adds a faint echo of trust to its record, so a Sybil operator must pay real compute and time for every fake identity, while honest agents accumulate standing. Over time these records form a nebula of interlinked work histories that is expensive to forge in bulk and cheap for peers to check.
